**What this PR does / why we need it**:
The NLB attributes are now reconciled immediately after creating the load balancer. Previously, the LB attributes related annotations were applied only during updates to the service object. This required a two step process to apply the attributes correctly.
**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
<!--
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.
_If PR is about `failing-tests or flakes`, please post the related issues/tests in a comment and do not use `Fixes`_*
-->
Fixes #81584
Fixes #82595

**Special notes for your reviewer**:
Tested on kops cluster by specifying the following annotations on a service, the load balancer type is 'nlb' - 
```
service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type
service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-cross-zone-load-balancing-enabled
service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-access-log-enabled
service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-access-log-s3-bucket-name
service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-access-log-s3-bucket-prefix
``` 
Test summary
- The annotation values get applied as expected during service creation
- If aws-load-balancer-access-log-enabled is set to false, the other bucket-name and bucket-prefix get ignored
- If service is created without the LB attributes annotations, default values are configured
- Modifying the annotations results in corresponding change to the LB attributes

issue_context.title: AWS: Network Load Balancer ignores annotations upon creation
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
Code for handling annotations for load balancer is executed only upon load balancer modification, not creation in all versions including master branch.

So, for example, it's not possible to enable cross-zone load balancing upon creation. Only create-then-update process works.
- [1.14.6](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.14.6/pkg/cloudprovider/providers/aws/aws_loadbalancer.go#L344)
- [1.15.3](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.15.3/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/aws/aws_loadbalancer.go#L326)
- [master](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/aws/aws_loadbalancer.go#L336)


**What you expected to happen**:
Annotations  should be parsed both upon creation and update of load balancer

Code, that parses annotations should be moved outside `else` block
- [1.14.6](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.14.6/pkg/cloudprovider/providers/aws/aws_loadbalancer.go#L179)
- [1.15.3](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.15.3/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/aws/aws_loadbalancer.go#L164)
- [master](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/aws/aws_loadbalancer.go#L174)

or duplicated in `if` block

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
1. create `Service.spec.type.LoadBalancer` with:
```yaml
annotations:
  service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
  service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-cross-zone-load-balancing-enabled: "true"
```
 cross-zone load balancing will be off

2. modify something in `Service` definition — CZLB will be on


**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.14.0—1.14.6, 1.15.0—1.15.3, master
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: AWS

I experienced this recently with 1.14.9 on EKS. A newly created NLB ignored `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-cross-zone-load-balancing-enabled`.
Can confirm this also appears on EKS 1.16

Can confirm this appears where using k8s 1.16 on kops. It would be phenomenal to get cross-zone load balancing and healthcheck configuration annotations available for the NLB load balancer types. Related: #86624

For anyone stumbling on this same issue and trying to ensure high-availability before the annotation features are implemented, I have confirmed that you can enable cross-zone load balancing manually via the AWS console and it appears to remain resilient to future service changes. Additionally, I have done some preliminary testing with the passive health checks for NLBs and it appears clusters can remain resilient to pod failures (assuming redundant pods are available) due to the passive health checking built-in to NLBs.

The health check fix merged in #94546 does not address this annotation when NLB is created
`  service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-cross-zone-load-balancing-enabled: "true"`
The annotation is applied only during edits. This needs to be fixed, please reopen this issue.

Since (looking at the [AWS SDK docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-go/api/service/elbv2/)) there is nowhere to include attributes in the [`c.elb.CreateLoadBalancer`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ef33126cc7a60da6799821a49cc9772479e86cf7/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/aws/aws_loadbalancer.go#L178)'s [`CreateLoadBalancerInput`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-go/api/service/elbv2/#CreateLoadBalancerInput) parameter, I guess this just requires calling `reconcileLBAttributes` after the `CreateLoadBalancer` call, as is done after the `// sync mappings` block in the modification path.

That suggests that this bug also affects the other [S3 Access Logs Attributes](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ef33126cc7a60da6799821a49cc9772479e86cf7/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/aws/aws_loadbalancer.go#L52-L54), too.
I'm also running into this issue as well, I don't know why this issue has been closed.

It was closed because it was inaccurately marked as fixed by #94546. Hopefully #95247 will land relatively quickly, and make it into the 1.20 release.

Edit: #95247 has merged, will be fixed in Kubernetes 1.20.
